text: Before the Passover festival, Jesus knew that his hour had come to leave this world and go to the Father. Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the very end.
During supper, the devil had already put it into the heart of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, to betray him.
Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come from God and was going back to God,
rose from the meal, laid aside his outer garments, took a towel, and tied it around his waist.
Then he poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples' feet, drying them with the towel he had around him.
He came to Simon Peter, who said to him, "Lord, are you going to wash my feet?"
Jesus answered him, "Right now you do not understand what I am doing, but later you will understand."

versions.text: Jesus answered him, "You do not understand what I am doing now, but later you will understand."
versions.explanation: In the Greek, ἄρτι ("now") modifies "you do not know," not "what I am doing." As it stands, the English can be misread as "what I am doing now," which shifts the sense. Placing "right now" at the front removes the ambiguity and keeps the contrast with "later" clear when read aloud.

text: Peter said to him, "You shall never wash my feet." Jesus answered, "Unless I wash you, you have no share with me."
Simon Peter said to him, "Lord, then not only my feet, but my hands and my head as well!"
Jesus said to him, "Anyone who has bathed needs only to wash his feet; his whole body is clean. And you are clean—though not all of you."
For he knew who was going to betray him; that is why he said, "Not all of you are clean."
When he had washed their feet, he put on his garments again, took his place at the table, and said to them, "Do you understand what I have done for you?
You call me Teacher and Lord, and you are right, for that is what I am.
So if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.
I have given you an example, so that you also should do as I have done for you.
Truly, truly, I tell you: no servant is greater than his master, and no messenger is greater than the one who sent him.
If you know these things, you are blessed when you do them.
I am not speaking of all of you. I know the ones I have chosen. But the Scripture must be fulfilled: 'The one who eats my bread has lifted his heel against me.'

versions.text: I am not speaking of all of you. I know the ones I have chosen. But the Scripture must be fulfilled: 'The one who ate my bread has lifted his heel against me.'
versions.explanation: ὁ τρώγων is a present participle ("the one who eats/shares my bread"), describing an ongoing table fellowship, in contrast with the aorist ἐπῆρεν ("has lifted"). The past-tense "ate" loses this deliberate contrast.

text: I am telling you now, before it happens, so that when it does happen you may believe that I am he.
Truly, truly, I tell you: whoever receives anyone I send receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me."
After saying this, Jesus was troubled in spirit and testified, "Truly, truly, I tell you: one of you will betray me."
The disciples looked at one another, at a loss to know which of them he meant.
Reclining next to Jesus was one of his disciples, the one whom Jesus loved.

versions.text: One of his disciples, the one Jesus loved, was reclining close beside him.
versions.explanation: As written, the pronouns "his" and "him" both come before the clarifying name, so a listener may momentarily take "him" to refer to the disciple rather than to Jesus. Naming Jesus first resolves the ambiguity and reads more smoothly aloud.

text: Simon Peter motioned to him to ask who it was he meant.
So he leaned back against Jesus and asked him, "Lord, who is it?"
Jesus answered, "It is the one to whom I give this piece of bread when I have dipped it." Then he dipped the bread and gave it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot.
As soon as Judas took the bread, Satan entered into him. Jesus said to him, "Do quickly what you are going to do."
No one at the table understood why he said this to him.
Since Judas kept the money box, some thought Jesus was telling him, "Buy what we need for the festival," or that he should give something to the poor.
So Judas took the bread and went out at once. And it was night.
When he had gone, Jesus said, "Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God has been glorified in him.

versions.text: When he had gone, Jesus said, "Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in him.
versions.explanation: ἐδοξάσθη is aorist passive; the perfect rendering "has been glorified" better conveys the decisive, accomplished sense that sets up the future verbs in the next verse. (If adopted, verse 32 should likewise read "If God has been glorified in him..." for consistency.)

text: If God is glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself—and will glorify him at once.
Little children, I am with you only a little longer. You will look for me, and as I told the Jews, so I tell you now: where I am going, you cannot come.
A new commandment I give you: love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another.
By this everyone will know that you are my disciples—if you have love for one another."
Simon Peter said to him, "Lord, where are you going?" Jesus answered, "Where I am going you cannot follow me now, but you will follow later."
Peter said, "Lord, why can't I follow you now? I will lay down my life for you."
Jesus answered, "You will lay down your life for me? Truly, truly, I tell you: before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times."
